claims.text: ProductsController.List() has a single return, Ok(products), with no branch on how many rows the query returned; it answers 200 regardless of the row count, including zero.
ProductsController.Get(int id) calls db.Products.FindAsync(id); if the result is null it returns NotFound() (404) before building any ProductDto, otherwise it returns Ok(new ProductDto(...)) (200).
Neither List() nor Get(int id) in ProductsController writes to the database; both only read via db.Products.
Sending GET /api/v1/products/1 to the running stage-1 lab returns 200 with one product's JSON; sending GET /api/v1/products/999999 returns 404 with no product in the body.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang stage-1 lab: curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/products/1 and /api/v1/products/999999

claims.text: By REST/HTTP convention, GET is a safe method: it must not change server state, a stronger guarantee than idempotence (which only concerns the effect of repeating the same call).
claims.source_hint: HTTP semantics convention (safe methods), independent of any one framework
